expectations: The response refuses to fall back to organization-wide scope.

evals.prompt: Can you give me the docker run command to pull the official kei-proxy image and run it as a sidecar service listening on a port?
evals.expected_output: Explains there is no public image; build kei-proxy:local from the Kei repo root. The one-shot CLI mode runs as a subprocess co-located with the harness. The daemon mode (kei-proxy serve) runs as a same-host daemon (bare metal) or same-container daemon (Docker), with an optional same-pod companion container on Kubernetes, over a Unix socket; it serves readiness, model routes, and a governed POST /v1/authorize decided locally by the runtime PDP. Do not expose a TCP port for governed calls outside the validated daemon contract (the authorize/session routes are socket-only).
expectations: The response does not invent a registry URL for a kei-proxy image.
The response distinguishes one-shot CLI (subprocess per call) from daemon mode (Unix socket; same-host or same-container daemon).
The response says the daemon serves a governed authorize route over the socket (local PDP), not that it is unavailable.
The response does not describe a network-exposed listener or TCP port for governed calls.

evals.prompt: What does kei runtime bootstrap do?
evals.expected_output: `kei runtime bootstrap` sends the installation credential to the control plane to register the runtime, gets back the installation status and workspace binding. It must show workspace_id for a valid installation. Run after credential rotation and after any configuration change. Run via kei-proxy runtime bootstrap on deployed runtimes.

evals.prompt: How do I pair a runtime with a harness?
evals.expected_output: `kei bot bind --installation INSTALLATION_ID` activates the runtime; it has no --harness flag. Desktop harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) are sessions of the installation and are paired with `kei harness sync`, with no `kei harness add`. Only a custom (SDK) harness is registered first with `kei harness add --kind custom --installation INSTALLATION_ID --agent AGENT_ID`, then synced.
expectations: says `kei harness add` is needed first only for a custom (SDK) harness

evals.expected_output: The runtime sends periodic heartbeats to the control plane to show it is alive and healthy. Running `kei bot status --installation INSTALLATION_ID` shows the last heartbeat time and the current status. A missing heartbeat indicates the runtime is down and governed calls will fail closed.
